categories.label: Onboarding and first run
categories.parity_gate: Fresh users can install, configure a provider/profile, diagnose errors, and obtain a first answer without manual state repair.
categories.surpass_gate: Zaion adds clear data, permission, cost, and trust previews plus safe migration from competing agents.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: At least 95 percent first-answer success across the supported OS/install matrix with median completion in three minutes or less.

categories.label: Terminal UI runtime
categories.parity_gate: The production TUI supports session lifecycle, streaming, queue, steer, interrupt, approval, clarify, recovery, and terminal restoration.
categories.surpass_gate: Signed provenance and risk controls are actionable without displacing the chat workflow.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Real PTY tests pass on supported platforms, randomized protocol sequences leave no corrupt state, and cancellation is visible within one second.

categories.label: Session, profile, and workspace continuity
categories.parity_gate: Profiles isolate config and state; sessions persist, search, resume, reset, branch, prune, export, and preserve compression lineage.
categories.surpass_gate: Principal-bound cross-channel continuity and handoff lineage are cryptographically verifiable.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: A ten-thousand-session stress and crash-recovery matrix has zero cross-principal leakage and no lost lineage.

categories.label: Agent tools and execution
categories.parity_gate: High-value web, terminal, file, browser, vision, todo, memory, code, delegation, cron, messaging, approval, and result-storage workflows are usable.
categories.surpass_gate: Every execution has typed terminal state, policy authority, environment identity, receipt, proof join, and live cancellation.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Twelve representative end-to-end workflow suites pass across required environments with no secret leak or unauthorized mutation.

categories.label: Skills and extension ecosystem
categories.parity_gate: Users can discover, inspect, install, update, disable, and invoke built-in and third-party skills through stable toolsets.
categories.surpass_gate: Skills have signed provenance, isolated execution, compatibility imports, evaluation, and rollback.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: At least fifty maintained third-party skills and one hundred representative tasks achieve at least 85 percent success with supply-chain negatives passing.

categories.label: Persistent memory
categories.parity_gate: Memory providers implement initialize, prefetch, queued recall, turn sync, session switch/end, pre-compression, delegation, tools, and shutdown.
categories.surpass_gate: Source-bound memory atoms expose conflict, expiry, invalidation, answer-span use, and user governance.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Declared recall benchmarks reach Recall@10 of at least 0.90 and precision of at least 0.85 with zero cross-principal contamination.

categories.label: Prompt assembly and context compression
categories.parity_gate: Identity, project rules, memory, skills, tools, platform overlays, and session context have deterministic precedence and safe long-session compression.
categories.surpass_gate: Context packs, compression lineage, and answer use are hash-bound and inspectable.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Two-hundred-turn suites preserve at least 95 percent of declared critical facts, save at least 50 percent of eligible tokens, and retain every tool pair.

categories.label: Gateway and browser control plane
categories.parity_gate: One production server owns HTTP, WebSocket, UI, session, stream, queue, approval, clarify, authentication, CORS, and health behavior.
categories.surpass_gate: Local-first zero-trust ingress and egress are signed, attributable, and replay-auditable.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Protocol fuzzing has no crash, one hundred concurrent sessions meet p95 event latency below 100 ms, and unauthorized write tests all fail closed.

categories.label: Messaging channels
categories.parity_gate: Supported channels implement identity, session routing, typing/edit/reaction, media, retry, topic/reply, pending merge, and owned cancellation.
categories.surpass_gate: Cross-channel handoff preserves one principal/session proof while unified policy remains platform-aware.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Five tier-one and ten additional channels pass contract tests; live smoke and a 72-hour soak show no lost or duplicate reply.

categories.label: Model Context Protocol
categories.parity_gate: MCP supports stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE, discovery, filters, resources, prompts, list_changed, sampling, parallel opt-in, OAuth, reconnect, and serving.
categories.surpass_gate: Each server has least-privilege policy, description scanning, process isolation, and signed receipts.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: MCP Inspector and at least twenty reference servers pass, refresh loses no valid tool, no orphan process remains, and protocol overhead stays below target.

categories.label: Agent Client Protocol
categories.parity_gate: ACP stdio supports new, load, resume, fork, list, cancel, history replay, permissions, tool progress, cwd, model switch, persistence, and MCP expansion.
categories.surpass_gate: Editor operations bind to Zaion capabilities and proofs and can hand off to other stable surfaces.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Three real ACP clients and one hundred lifecycle scenarios pass with protocol-clean stdout, isolated cwd, and cancel response below one second.

categories.label: Execution environments
categories.parity_gate: Local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, managed cloud, Daytona, and Vercel-style sandboxes share execution, file sync, persistent shell, timeout, and cleanup contracts.
categories.surpass_gate: Every backend has a strong signed environment identity, policy decision, reproducible receipt, and visible result storage.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Seven backend classes pass at least twenty common scenarios each, leak no resource after timeout, and pass the sandbox escape suite.

categories.label: Batch, trajectory, and evaluation
categories.parity_gate: Batch execution provides worker isolation, checkpoints, resume, toolset sampling, trajectories, compression, metrics, timeouts, and SWE-style runners.
categories.surpass_gate: Trajectories are signed, reproducible, cost-budgeted, and promotion-gated by independent evaluation.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: A ten-thousand-task interruption run loses or duplicates no task, all provenance verifies, and cost-adjusted quality exceeds the pinned baseline by at least 10 percent.

categories.label: Release and operations
categories.parity_gate: Public source, tags, installers, packages, containers, services, update, uninstall, CI, checksums, security policy, and recovery are verified.
categories.surpass_gate: A reproducible Rust artifact materially reduces startup, memory, and operational complexity with measured evidence.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Clean-machine install, upgrade, rollback, and service smoke pass on supported platforms for three consecutive releases with signed artifacts and SBOMs.

categories.label: Documentation and community
categories.parity_gate: Public docs, migration guides, contribution/security processes, examples, extension discovery, and release communication are current.
categories.surpass_gate: A compatible, signed extension ecosystem publishes transparent product evidence and lowers migration cost.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: At least twenty external contributors, fifty third-party skills, three months of releases, median issue first response below 72 hours, and 85 percent documentation task success are evidenced.

categories.label: Hero mission: dev/SRE vertical loop
categories.parity_gate: Issue/alert to investigation, code/config change, approval, execution, verification, rollback capability, and signed evidence pack completes end to end without manual repair.
categories.surpass_gate: Approval, steer/interrupt, diff/test/rollback, and evidence cards are actionable in the live workflow; rollback restores known-good state.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: First real mission under 15 minutes; 100 percent of successful missions are verifiable with zero silent failures; cancel p95 under 250ms.

categories.label: Reliability and security chaos
categories.parity_gate: Duplicate requests, crash at each event-commit point, out-of-order events, disconnect/reconnect, provider timeout/429/malformed, approval timeout/denied, process-tree cancel, disk full, signature tampering, cross-tenant IDOR, sandbox escape, upgrade interruption and rollback are all handled without corruption.
categories.surpass_gate: Failures are structured, user-visible, auditable; ledger RPO=0 RTO<60s; no double side effects.
categories.ten_out_of_ten: Required chaos scenarios pass with zero data loss or cross-tenant leakage; recovery and evidence invariants hold under fault injection.
